factor: a. Deaths of DNI holders not purged
base_y_supuestos: Expected deaths in the 3,033,786 stock at 2022 Argentine age-sex death rates (DEIS defweb22 deaths / INDEC 2022 projected population) applied to the digitized age structure = 37,809/yr, crude 12.46 per 1,000, with 53% of them at 80+. Arithmetic ceiling if NOTHING were purged 2009-2022 = 270k-418k. The data cap it far below that: RENAPER 80+ = 138,947 vs census 80+ = 107,926, ratio 1.29. Since 53% of deaths fall at 80+, an unpurged mass of U implies the true live ratio at 80+ is (138,947 - 0.53U)/107,926; U=120,000 already forces that ratio down to 0.71, below any plausible value given the all-origin ratio is 1.57 and Italy's 1.30. Mechanism evidence points both ways: AGN Informe 216/2013 s.4.4.3 found a ~6-month processing delay and that before elections only voting-age nationals were processed, 'dejando para su posterior procesamiento los extranjeros'; RENAPER Disp. 1804/2018 considerandos concede 'atrasos' by provincial registries; RENAPER's own convenio disclaims that it 'no garantiza el cumplimiento ... en la remision tempestiva'; and deaths abroad of foreign nationals have NO notification channel at all (consular registration excludes non-nationals). Against that: every source line says 'personas vivas', and the age profile of the excess is the inverse of a mortality signature. Note deaths abroad add no term beyond factor b - the person had already emigrated - but they make that over-count permanently irreversible.

factor: b. Emigration / non-residence not caught by the 6-month DNM filter
base_y_supuestos: The dominant term, and a residual: b = gap + c + e - a - f - g - h. Independent lower-bound check from the age profile: excess over a reference ratio of 1.30-1.35 (the ratio observed at ages 70-89, where mobility is lowest) = 460,000-547,000; this understates b because it assumes zero mobility excess among the elderly. Second independent check: RENAPER itself removed 563,333 records by Aug 2024 and 683,970 by Jun 2025 with no published methodological note. Mechanism: the filter deletes only people DNM RECORDS as absent >6 months; foreigners frequently exit on a non-Argentine document and are never matched (Ameijeiras 2025), land borders with Paraguay/Bolivia/Chile record poorly, and circular migrants returning inside 6 months are always retained. INDEC AD39 Tabla 11 puts emigration of non-natives 2010-2022 at 181,779, but that is a CENSUS RESIDUAL (2022 stock minus survivors of the 2010 stock minus arrivals) and so cannot be used to explain a census-register gap without circularity.

Excludes Libreta Civica, Libreta de Enrolamiento and DNI tapa verde/bordo (p.7). Should bite hardest on elderly Europeans. It does not show up: RENAPER Europe = 212,365 (7.0% of 3,033,786, p.24) vs census Europe = 145,776, a ratio of 1.46 against an all-origin ratio of 1.57 - a mild relative deficit only. Census European-born aged 65+ = 108,313 (Italy 61,647 = 90% of Italian-born; Spain 33,571 = 69%). Since DNI renewal is compulsory at 5/8/14 years and required to vote, draw a pension or use public health care, the residual stock of manual documents in 2022 is small. Range reflects that the effect is real in direction but not separately identifiable in the data.

factor: d. Date difference 18 May -> 31 Aug 2022 (3.45 months)
base_y_supuestos: Two offsetting terms of similar size. Net non-native migration from INDEC AD39 Tabla 11 = +440,455 over 2010-2022 = 33,881/yr -> +9,741 over the interval. Expected deaths in the foreign-born stock over the same interval = -10,870. Net = -1,129. AD39 notes the TOTAL balance turns negative in 2021-2022, driven by native emigration, so the non-native term is if anything smaller. Cannot plausibly account for more than about 1% of the gap.

factor: e. Irregular migrants and DNI-in-process (counted by census, not by RENAPER)
base_y_supuestos: The report concedes this itself (p.3-4): 'puede haber personas que no cuenten actualmente con DNI argentino, ya sea porque esta en tramite, cuenta con un antiguo DNI o esta en condiciones de irregularidad'. Best empirical anchor: ENMA (Encuesta Nacional Migrante de Argentina). ENMA 2020 found 11% of surveyed migrants without a DNI; ENMA 2023 finds 7% ('el porcentaje de personas migrantes que tiene DNI es elevado (93%), incluso superior al registrado en la ENMA 2020 (89%)'). The May/Aug 2022 reference date sits between the two, so 7-11% of a true resident stock near 2.0M gives 137,000-226,000. Note that 'without DNI' is the right concept here, NOT 'irregular': RENAPER misses anyone lacking a digital DNI whatever their legal status, and ENMA reports about half of its no-DNI group is legally regular (precaria 31.7%, temporaria awaiting DNI 16.8%, documento provisorio 5.9%) - which is exactly the precaria/transitoria population excluded by Ley 25.871 art. 30. Range widened upward because ENMA is a non-probability sample and concedes 'la mencionada fuente tiene sesgos para captar poblacion en situacion de irregularidad documentaria'. Concentration by origin (ENMA 2023): extra-MERCOSUR non-European 13.5%, extra-MERCOSUR European 6.8%, MERCOSUR 6.1%; by region NOA 24.0% and NEA 23.3% vs AMBA 5.8%. This factor works AGAINST the gap.

Largely a non-issue. Both sources classify by PLACE OF BIRTH, so naturalized Argentines born abroad are in both, and Italian/Spanish dual nationals born in Argentina are in neither. RENAPER's later open data confirms the register keeps pais_nacimiento and nacionalidad as separate fields (Jun 2026: 2,367,573 born abroad vs 2,147,086 of foreign nationality). Residual risk: Argentine citizens BORN ABROAD to Argentine parents, registered through consulates, who hold a DNI with an Argentine domicile while living abroad - these would inflate RENAPER only. The age profile argues this is small: the RENAPER/census ratio at ages 0-4 is 0.38 and at 5-19 only 1.19-1.37, well below the all-age 1.57.

factor: g. Census universe is PRIVATE DWELLINGS only
base_y_supuestos: 1,933,463 is 'poblacion en viviendas particulares'. CORRECTED UNIVERSE: the DEFINITIVE census total is 45,892,285 = 45,618,787 in private dwellings + 267,793 in collective dwellings + 5,705 in situacion de calle, so 273,498 people sit outside the published universe. (An earlier draft used 425,916, taken from the PROVISIONAL January 2023 count of 46,044,703 - that figure is superseded.) At the 4.24% national foreign-born share that is 11,596; at 2-3x over-representation 23,193-34,789. Bottom-up: collective dwellings are 40.0% prisons (107,173) and 30.6% geriatric homes (82,016); the foreign-born are heavily aged (20.4% are 65+, and 90% of Italian-born and 69% of Spanish-born are 65+), so 10-15% of geriatric residents (8,200-12,300) plus 5-8% of the prison population (5,400-8,600) is a reasonable order. CRITICAL: INDEC asked place of birth on the collective-dwelling questionnaire (qq. 12 and 14) but has NEVER PUBLISHED the foreign-born count for that universe; the public Redatam collective base exposes only sex and age. So 1,933,463 is a lower bound whose deficit is bounded above by 273,498 but is otherwise unmeasured. This is a universe difference, not an error in either source.

factor: h. Census under-enumeration of the foreign-born
base_y_supuestos: INDEC AD39 (Tabla 4, p.18) publishes a NET population differential of -0.5% for 2022 overall, -2.1% for men and +1.1% for women, and explicitly declines to publish an omission rate ('modificaciones metodologicas y conceptuales impiden realizar una comparacion directa entre los calculos de la omision censal de censos previos y el Censo 2022'). No migrant-specific figure exists for 2022. At national rates the foreign-born deficit would be 9,667 (total) to 18,313 (men). The high end comes from the SEX-RATIO discrepancy: census foreign-born F/M = 1.217 vs RENAPER 1.070; holding the census female count fixed and imposing RENAPER's ratio implies 119,725 foreign-born men missing from the census. Calvelo (2011) is the standard Argentine reference that non-native omission always exceeds native omission and has risen since 1960; prior-census omission was 2.75% (2001) and 1.99% (2010).
Identidad contable: brecha = (a + b + f + g + h) - (c + e). Los factores c y e reducen RENAPER frente al censo, de modo que los factores inflacionarios deben sumar MAS que la brecha observada.
